source.title: Impact of Deep Learning Optimizers and Hyperparameter Tuning on the Performance of Bearing Fault Diagnosis

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size effects on bearing-fault CNNs, extending batch-size generalization evidence to a new application setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out accuracy across batch sizes and optimizers, but does not report training error or the training–test gap. Results cited from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out classification accuracy across batch sizes 16, 64 and 128 under a fixed 100-epoch budget, extending V5 to bearing-fault classification. Training–test gaps are unnecessary for this comparison, although no workload-dependent batch threshold is established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that batch-size effects depend on learning rate and momentum, with larger batches favored at higher values and smaller batches at lower values. They also identify these hyperparameters as major performance determinants and TICNN as the strongest candidate for computational efficiency and noise robustness.
record.recipe_differences: Bearing-fault CNN classification on CWRU and MFPT; 100 training epochs, optimizer hyperparameter tuning, and noise-free/noisy test evaluation. Does not measure training–test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch-size effects vary with dataset and model; optimizer learning rate and momentum factor also affect performance.

fits_no_version.finding: All models exceeded 95% average noise-free test accuracy in the refined search, without reported batch-specific differences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tuned bearing-fault classifiers achieve high noise-free held-out accuracy.

record.problems: The study reports test accuracy but not training error, so it cannot measure the training–test gap. Batch-size results are primarily shown in figures; numeric values are not given in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The figures show separate model, optimizer, and batch-size results, but their numeric values are figure-only and the supplied text does not describe each combination. Aggregate-by-dataset figure rows were retained; no per-model values were reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label training and held-out accuracy.
Width variation beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
A directional adaptive-versus-SGD generalization comparison under limited versus broader tuning. The statement that no optimizer wins across models does not establish this comparison.

Language modeling and natural-image benchmarks; the workload-dependent batch threshold; longer training, warmup, learning-rate scaling, and normalization or regularization interventions. Noise-free refined-search results lack batch-specific contrasts.
A controlled dropout intervention. Comparisons involving TICNN also change architecture and do not isolate dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.

missing.what: Initial-search batch-size interactions: larger batches generally performed better at high learning rates, while smaller batches performed better at low rates. High momentum also disadvantaged small batches in several comparisons. These explicit textual results are distinct from the declared omission of figure-only numerical combinations.
missing.locator: Section IV-A, discussion of Figs. 11–15; Section IV-B, discussion of Figs. 17–22; Conclusion

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its noisy-test comparisons measure robustness to added Gaussian noise, extending the original benchmark settings. No figure values, effect sizes, or significance claims can be reconstructed from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization gap on the specified image and language benchmarks.
Image-classification and language-model settings; comparison at a workload-dependent batch threshold; large-batch results under adapted recipes such as warmup or longer training.
Dropout intervention and its effect on test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training–test gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting test accuracy.
